# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

# Memory Index

- [Post-0.10.2 Plan](project_post_0_10_2_plan.md) — Open work after the 0.10.2 release lives in .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md (local only, never PR it): 12 workstreams, parallel lanes, stacked PRs, owner decisions (D01 blocks MATURIN/OWNER).
- [Prove With the Real Tool](feedback_prove_with_the_real_tool.md) — Fake-tool tests and clean compiles hid the 0.10.1 gh credential regression; reproduce auth/release/registry paths with the real tool, test the failing case first, state what is unproven.
- [Callisto Self-Release Incident — Durable Memory](project_release_self_hosting_incident_2026-09.md) — Claude invented and later misattributed the release approval gate, misunderstood rerun semantics, and repeatedly declared fixes before publication; records non-negotiable policy, verified failures, corrective architecture, and required incident protocol.
- [Hardcoded Values — Proactive Search Required](feedback_hardcoded_values.md) — User repeatedly frustrated by missed hardcoded values; always include a dedicated pass in any audit or fix session.
- [Track 0: gix WASI spike — NO-GO verdict](project_track0_wasi_verdict.md) — mmap ENOSYS in WASI blocks all gix object reads; callisto-moon exec-seam must use warpgate_pdk::exec_command.
- [Publish Pipeline Audit — 38 bugs, fix ordering, semantic coupling map](project_publish_pipeline_audit.md) — Full adversarial audit complete; 5 P0s, 11 P1s, 15+ P2s; three root patterns; phased fix sequence with dependency order.
- [Parallel Fixing Anti-Pattern](feedback_parallel_fixing.md) — Parallel agents for fixes fail on semantically coupled systems even across different files; use parallel for investigation only.
- [Validate Each Fix Individually](feedback_validate_each_fix.md) — Run targeted tests after every individual fix; do not batch changes and rely solely on final CI run.
- Architecture: ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/architecture/ (moved from .claude/semantic-model on 2026-09-25) — read before implementation work.
- [Active Work](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md) — Tracks B, E, F (resolve_package_config), G (callisto matrix) all shipped and passing just ci. Pipeline: canon→vector→lambda.
- [Canon Pipeline Scope](feedback_canon_pipeline_scope.md) — Skip canon ceremony for targeted bug fixes with RED tests already written; canon auditor loops infinitely on implementation-detail prose.
- [Workspace Audit 2026-08](project_workspace_audit_2026-08.md) — CLOSED: 8-dimension audit, all critical/high + all 31 medium/low findings re-verified fixed as of 2026-08-27.
- [Found Code Needs Same Rigor](feedback_found_code_needs_same_rigor.md) — Committing pre-existing uncommitted code after only "compiles + existing tests pass" missed a zero-test-coverage regression; found/inherited code needs the same TDD/adversarial rigor as freshly-written code.
- [Manifest Persist Track](project_manifest_persist_track.md) — Both Spec A (mutate/persist split) and Spec B (write-batching) shipped; the apply_version_plan redundant-open/persist audit finding is fully closed.
- [Reviewer Must Actually Run Checks](feedback_reviewer_must_actually_run_checks.md) — lambda-reviewer falsely reported clippy clean once; always instruct review agents to run commands for real, not infer results.
- [Iterate Reviews in Foreground](feedback_iterate_reviews_in_foreground.md) — Background agent notifications were unreliable across a multi-round spec/plan review loop; user called it out twice — run tight revise-review cycles in the foreground.
- [PR #5 Release Pipeline Hardening](project_pr5_release_pipeline_hardening.md) — Fixed-group max-severity-wins config + no-compounding test, plus SPEC-005 ReleaseEntry.is_prerelease shipped end to end; all CI green.
- [Track 7: Revwalk Bounding + Git Fixture Hermeticity Gap](project_git_fixture_hermeticity_gap.md) — nextest+global gpgsign causes ~120s hangs across ~13 test files; deferred as its own future track.
- [Diagnose, Don't Guess, Environment Issues](feedback_diagnose_dont_guess_environment_issues.md) — User rejected an unverified guess (XProtect); always confirm root cause with a falsifiable test before reporting it.
- [Recover Stale Agent Results After Session Interruption](feedback_recover_stale_agent_results.md) — Read the raw .output JSONL transcript directly when ListAgents/TaskOutput shows "completed" but the result looks like a stale mid-flight placeholder, instead of re-dispatching duplicates.
- [Always Use Plugins](feedback_always_use_plugins.md) — Route PR/commit narration and audits through courier/ranger/etc. plugin agents by default, not freehand, even when I already have full context.
- [Terse Comments Only](feedback_terse_comments.md) — One short line max, only for non-obvious WHY; stop writing multi-line prose comments in code/config even though CLAUDE.md already says this.
- [Cargo Slowness Root Cause](project_cargo_slowness_target_pollution.md) — Hours-long builds were a polluted target/debug (1.7M .o files); wipe it, split-debuginfo=off, one invocation shape, no parallel builds; cold build is 31 s.
- [No Red-Green, Lean Tokens](feedback_no_red_green_lean_tokens.md) — User dropped red-green testing and wants lean token spend; no heavy agent gating loops; CLI product tag callisto@{version} is intentional.
- [PR #101 Hardening State](project_pr101_hardening_state.md) — 7 local unpushed commits fix the audited release-lifecycle defects; deferred structural work, unverified-on-GitHub items, and the git add -u lesson.
- [Never Hard-Wrap Prose](feedback_never_hard_wrap_prose.md) — PR descriptions and all Markdown: one line per paragraph, never manual line breaks.
- [Succinct Written Artifacts](feedback_succinct_written_artifacts.md) — Changesets, PR bodies, docs: short, plain, no AI slop or backstory.
- [No Session Links](feedback_no_session_links.md) — Never put claude.ai session URLs/Claude-Session trailers in commits or PRs; public repo, private sessions.
- [Verify Before Recommending](feedback_verify_before_recommending.md) — Check code, callers and sibling repos before presenting any recommendation; audit findings are leads, not conclusions.
- [No Thin ADRs](feedback_no_thin_adrs.md) — ADRs only for significant decisions, with rejected options, enforcement and revisit triggers; process rules aren't ADRs.
- [Budget: Lean Pipeline](feedback_budget_lean_pipeline.md) — weekly token budget; leanest pipeline that still catches bugs; no cleanup agents or rework the user has to review.
- [Use gh stack](feedback_use_gh_stack.md) — stacked PRs must be native GitHub stacks (gh stack link); plain chained PRs get no CI.
- [Agent Context Briefs](feedback_agent_context_briefs.md) — curated 2-4k token briefs, one agent per PR via SendMessage, small fixes directly; no forks of long sessions.
- [Local Tracking, Not PRs](feedback_local_tracking_not_prs.md) — Tracking/handoff plans live in .claude/plans/ (git-excluded); never commit or PR them (PR #201 was closed for this).
- [Worktree Guard Command Shapes](feedback_worktree_guard_commands.md) — worktree-isolated sessions refuse heredocs, compound commands and text naming git; use /usr/bin/git and scripts written with the Write tool.

name: bug-hunter
description: >-

---

# Universal Rust Bug-Hunter Skill

## Goal

Find real bugs before they ship in any Rust repository (monorepos, CLI engines, libraries, polyglot WASM plugins): silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, data corruption, ordering staleness, crash-safety violations, and edge cases that break production.

This skill is **Rigid**: follow it exactly across any Rust workspace.

## The Law

> NO FINDING MARKED `CONFIRMED` WITHOUT AN END-TO-END TRACE. NO FIX MARKED DONE WITHOUT A TEST THAT FAILED BEFORE THE FIX AND PASSES AFTER, RUN IN THIS SESSION.

## Core Rules

- **Verify by Tracing**: Don't trust a comment, docstring, passing test, or a prior audit's "FIXED" label. Trace the code execution path yourself.
- **Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning**: When executing multi-agent bug hunts, DO NOT partition subagents by directory or crate names. ALWAYS partition subagents by **Hazard Taxonomy** or **Code Smell Sweep** across the entire workspace.
- **Strict Invariants**: Prioritize data integrity, crash-safety, error propagation, and security bugs over style or refactoring.
- **Read-Only Investigation**: Investigate and report findings first. Do not mutate files unless explicitly requested to apply fixes.

---

## The 6 Universal Rust Hazard Taxonomies

1. **Discarded Data & Unused CLI / Struct Parameters**: Leading-underscore parameters (`_opts`, `_config`), unused Clap CLI flags.
2. **Ordering, Mutability & Fixpoint Staleness**: First-write-wins vs max-value-wins, graph solver loops missing re-enqueueing logic.
3. **Spec-vs-Code Compliance Drift**: Requirements in design docs/specs missing enforcement logic in functions.
4. **Silent Fallbacks & Falsified Defaults**: Catch-all `unwrap_or` defaults hiding invalid state, swallowed I/O errors.
5. **Boundary Inputs & Format Edge Cases**: UTF-8 BOM (`\u{FEFF}`), CRLF line endings, unicode paths, detached HEAD Git states.
6. **Crash-Safety & Subprocess Security**: Atomic writes missing `.flush()` or `.sync_all()`, subprocess argument ordering.

---

## The 6 Architectural Code Smells & Ripgrep Sweeps

1. **Raw String Identity Smell**: `entry.name == pkg.id.to_string()` (Mismatched bare vs prefixed string comparison).
2. **Un-Transactional Disk Mutation Smell**: Step-by-step file edits without atomic batch rollback.
3. **Lossy Serde / CST Formatting Smell**: Replacing TOML/JSON nodes without preserving `.decor()` or line endings.
4. **Un-Fsynced Directory Metadata Smell**: `create_dir_all` or `atomic_write` missing parent directory `sync_all()`.
5. **Scopeless Fallback & Unbounded Traversal Smell**: Unbounded `revwalk` commit loops or catch-all `unwrap_or_else` defaults.
6. **Hardcoded Constant Dummy Smell**: Inserting placeholder strings (`"Release update"`, `"changeset.md"`) masking user metadata.

---

## 7 Shared Trait Centralization Framework

When auditing multi-crate workspaces, map recurring defects directly to 7 Centralized Rust Traits:
1. `PackageIdentityResolver`: Cross-ecosystem package matching and bare name resolution.
2. `VersionSpecRenderer`: Format & precision-preserving version requirement rendering.
3. `ChangesetStorage`: Crash-safe, transactional disk engine with parent directory fsync.
4. `CstManifestEditor`: CST format-preserving manifest modification (`toml_edit` and `serde_json`).
5. `GitVcsProvider`: Safe Git tags, shallow checkout handling, and bounded revwalk.
6. `CascadeSolver`: Fixpoint dependency graph solver & convergence tracking.
7. `ReportPresenter`: Unified text & JSON report renderer with rich `miette` diagnostic cards.

---

## Hazard-Taxonomy Multi-Agent Dispatch Matrix

| Agent Role | Scope | Objective |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`bug-hunter-scanner-rust`** | Taxonomies 1 & 4 | Scan workspace for unused CLI flags, discarded parameters, and silent `unwrap_or` defaults. |
| **`bug-hunter-adversary-rust`** | Taxonomies 2 & 3 | Trace execution paths end-to-end, disprove candidate signals, and check graph solver fixpoints and spec drift. |
| **`bug-hunter-remediator-rust`** | Taxonomies 5 & 6 | Audit boundary inputs, atomic write `.flush()`/`.sync_all()`, write failing regression tests (red), apply fixes. |
| **`bug-hunter-architect-rust`** | Smells 1-6 & Trait Centralization | Analyze recurring defect patterns, cluster code smells, and design lean Rust traits with formal contracts. |
| **`bug-hunter-mutator-rust`** | Mutation Testing & Coverage | Run `cargo-mutants`, find survived mutant branches, and write boundary unit tests ensuring assertions fail when code is mutated. |

---

## Evaluation Output Standard

Report each confirmed finding in this standard technical format:

```markdown
### [Severity: Critical | High | Medium | Low] <Brief Vulnerability Title>

- **Status**: CONFIRMED (execution path fully traced, file:line cited) | PLAUSIBLE (strong signal, not fully traced)
- **Location**: `path/to/file.rs:L123-L135`
- **Classification**: [Discarded Parameter | Fixpoint Staleness | Spec Drift | Silent Fallback | Boundary Condition | I/O Safety]
- **Root Cause**: Concise explanation of the flaw in the current implementation logic.
- **Failing Scenario**: Concrete payload, CLI command, or input state that triggers the defect.
- **Verification Strategy**: A test that fails on current code and passes once fixed.
```

- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

1	# Bug-Hunter Findings Ledger
2	
3	Append-only log of findings from prior bug-hunter runs. Check this before starting a new sweep so you don't re-spend budget rediscovering the same bug. Update an entry's `Fix Status` in place when it changes — don't delete history, mark it.
4	
5	Format: one entry per confirmed finding. `Fix Status: unfixed | fix applied, untested | fixed (test run + date)`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	### [Medium] PEP 735 Dependency Groups declared supported in spec, entirely unimplemented in code
10	- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-03 sweep)
11	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:183-256` (`iter_dependencies`), `:258-343` (`update_dependency_spec`); spec: `docs/04-python-engine-spec.md:14`
12	- **Classification**: Spec Drift
13	- **Root Cause**: The Python engine spec lists PEP 735 (`[dependency-groups]`) as one of 5 core PEPs supported. `python.rs` only reads/writes `[project].dependencies` and `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` — no code anywhere references `dependency-groups`.
14	- **Failing Scenario**: A `pyproject.toml` with `[dependency-groups] test = ["pytest>=7.0"]` pinning an in-workspace sibling — a cascade-triggering bump never rewrites the entry, invisible to cascade/validate/version alike.
15	- **Fix Status**: unfixed — spec-correction/spec-completion pass dispatched 2026-08-03, code fix not yet started, pending that pass landing.
16	
17	### [Critical→fixed] `status`/`plan-publish`/`validate` all crashed on the wasm path — `tags.rs` had no CommandRunner fallback
18	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, real end-to-end wasm sandbox regression test)
19	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (`last_tag_for`, `TagIndex::build`)
20	- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap
21	- **Root Cause**: `last_tag_for` took an unused `_runner: &R` (`CommandRunner`) parameter and unconditionally called `callisto_vcs::GitRepository::discover(root)?` (gix, native-only). On `wasm32`, `discover` always returns `Err`, so this propagated straight up through `TagIndex::build` and killed `Workspace::load` on the very first package for any real moon invocation — before any actual git logic ran. Found by direct re-reading of `tags.rs`/`changed.rs` after the architecture discussion concluded gix must stay native-only; `changed.rs` already had the correct gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape, `tags.rs` never did.
22	- **Fix**: `fetch_all_tags` (new) tries gix first, falls through (not `?`) to one `runner.run("git", &["tag","--list"], root)` call when unavailable — mirroring `changed.rs`'s existing pattern exactly, so no new design was invented. Glob-matching against the raw tag list now happens in `callisto-graph` itself (mirroring `callisto-vcs`'s `globset` semantics exactly), so tag selection is byte-identical regardless of which path sourced the list. `TagIndex::build` now fetches the tag list once and reuses it across all packages (was: once per package) — fixes both the wasm32 crash and the O(N) host-round-trip performance gap flagged in the architecture discussion.
23	- **Verification**: reproduced the crash pre-fix through the real compiled `.wasm` under a real wasmtime sandbox (`exit_code: 1`, `E_GRAPH`, "gix native git operations disabled on WASM target"), confirmed `exit_code: 0` with the correct `lastTag` post-fix — genuine end-to-end evidence, not just a unit test. Also added a call-counting test proving the N→1 batching.
24	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
25	
26	### [Medium→fixed] `Version::deserialize` was hardcoded to `VersionGrammar::SemVer`, silently broken for PEP-440-only strings
27	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — the earlier deferral was revisited with real investigation, not just implemented blind
28	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs`
29	- **Classification**: Spec Drift
30	- **Investigation**: grepped every real serde-deserialization call site for a `Version`-bearing type; found exactly one with no available grammar signal — `commands/tag.rs`'s `PublishPlan` ingestion (reads a plan file/stdin from a potentially separate process/CI step, no sibling ecosystem field). Confirmed no PEP-440 `Version` reaches that path *today* (`plan_publish` has no `PublishTarget::Pypi` branch yet), but PyPI/PEP 440 is a fully live, non-stub ecosystem elsewhere in the codebase (manifest parsing, bump logic, and the publish-client classifier are all already implemented) — so this was going to silently break the moment that wiring gap closed.
31	- **Fix**: `Version::deserialize` now tries `SemVer` first (strictest/most unambiguous), falls back to `Pep440` only if that fails — mirroring `VersionReq::deserialize`'s existing multi-grammar pattern. Residual ambiguity (a string valid under both grammars always resolves to SemVer) is documented directly on the impl and pinned by a test, matching the same accepted tradeoff `VersionReq` already carries.
32	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
33	
34	### [High→fixed] `cargo.rs` silently dropped BOM on write despite a comment claiming it was handled
35	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
36	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs`
37	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback (same class as the earlier CST-fidelity fixes; this instance was missed because a code comment incorrectly claimed `toml_edit` handled it internally — that claim was true for the read path, false for the write path)
38	- **Root Cause**: `CargoToml::open` stripped the BOM before parsing but never recorded that fact; `persist()` wrote `self.document.to_string()` with no BOM restoration.
39	- **Fix**: Added `has_bom: bool`, populated on open, prepended back on `persist()` — mirrors `python.rs`'s existing pattern. Note: `WorkspaceCargoResolver`'s separate load/persist path was NOT covered by this fix and may have the same latent gap for a workspace-root `Cargo.toml` with a BOM — flagged, not verified either way.
40	- **Fix Status**: fixed (for `CargoToml` directly; `WorkspaceCargoResolver` unverified).
41	
42	### [High→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam didn't route a missing-binary host-abort through its own promised `Result` — affected both `execute_extension` and `initialize_extension`
43	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
44	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
45	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback / Crash-Safety (falsifies the crate's own "never panics, every failure caught into the report" claim)
46	- **Root Cause**: When the target program (`moon`/`git`) can't be resolved, `warpgate` 0.30.5's host-side `exec_command` closure returns `Err` from *native* code — Extism aborts the entire plugin call rather than routing it back into the guest as a value the guest's own `Result` handling can see. `MoonCommandRunner::run`'s `Err(e) => classify_host_failure(...)` branch never ran; the whole host call failed instead.
47	- **Fix**: Pre-check existence via `warpgate_pdk::command_exists` (shells to `which`, not the target program, so a missing program yields an ordinary `false`) before calling `exec`, turning it into the clean `CommandError::NotFound` the method already promised.
48	- **Fix Status**: fixed. Found only because the new black-box failure-path tests (dispatched to close a coverage gap) immediately falsified the "never panics" claim on first write — exactly the kind of bug happy-path-only testing had been hiding.
49	
50	### [High→fixed] `callisto add --dry-run` didn't apply `--dry-run` at all — wrote to disk anyway
51	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (live-tested pre- and post-fix against the built CLI, both text and JSON output formats)
52	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/add.rs`
53	- **Classification**: Unchecked Flag (same class as the original, already-fixed `version --dry-run` bug — recurred in a sibling command)
54	- **Fix**: computes and reports the would-be changeset content/path (both output formats) without calling `atomic_write`/`create_dir_all` when `global.dry_run` is set.
55	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
56	
57	### [Medium→fixed] `callisto publish`'s output couldn't distinguish "computed a plan" from "actually published packages"
58	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
59	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs`, new `callisto_model::report::PublishReport`
60	- **Classification**: UX / Missing Feature
61	- **Fix**: new `PublishReport` type (following the codebase's existing `Plan`-vs-`Report` naming convention) carries per-package `PublishAttempt`/outcome; `PublishOrchestrator::execute` now returns it instead of `()`; the CLI's real (non-dry-run) path prints/returns it instead of re-rendering the input plan.
62	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
63	
64	### [Low→fixed] `CliError::Io`/`CliError::Registry` lacked `help()` text, inconsistent with `NotATty`'s pattern
65	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
66	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/error.rs`
67	- **Fix**: `Io` converted to a struct variant carrying the failing path (with a manual `From<std::io::Error>` preserving `?`-ergonomics at call sites with no natural path), both variants now have actionable `help()` text. Verified with a real before/after repro (`callisto tag --plan /nonexistent/plan.json`).
68	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
69	
70	### [Critical→fixed] `commands/tag.rs`'s `create_tags_with_options` hard-crashed on wasm — same bug class as the original tags.rs crash, not actually fixed everywhere
71	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (found via exhaustive call-site audit of `GitRepository::discover` prompted by finding the first instance in `tags.rs`)
72	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs`
73	- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap (same class as the already-fixed `tags.rs` bug)
74	- **Fix**: gix-discovered once at the top of the function; new `tag_exists` (read, gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback, mirrors `tags.rs`) and mutating fallbacks for `create_tag` (`git tag -a`, annotated, no-force) and `create_floating_major` (`git tag -f`, matching gix's exact current semantics) — but for the mutating paths, a real gix failure on a real repo is NOT masked by retrying through the shell (fallback only fires when gix was never discovered at all, not on a genuine gix error).
75	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
76	
77	### [High→fixed] `callisto-conventional`'s `fetch_commits` discarded its `CommandRunner` param — silently dropped conventional-commit inference on wasm
78	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
79	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`
80	- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter
81	- **Fix**: gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback (mirroring `tags.rs`), new `fetch_commits_via_command_runner` shelling `git log --no-merges --format=\x1e%H\x1f%B <range> [-- <pathspecs>]` (RS/US control-char field separators, immune to misparsing multi-line commit messages; avoided `-z`/NUL-termination since it needs git ≥2.34, above this repo's declared `>=2.20` floor). A malformed/unparseable line now returns `ConventionalError::MalformedGitLogOutput` (a previously-dead-code variant) instead of silently dropping the commit.
82	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
83	
84	### [Medium→fixed] `aggregate.rs`'s own `resolve_since` had no `CommandRunner` fallback either — silently degraded to unbounded full-history walk on wasm
85	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
86	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs`
87	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
88	- **Fix**: same gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet <tag>^{commit}`), preserving the existing invariant that a real gix `Ok` result (even `Ok(None)`) is authoritative and the `CommandRunner` is never touched when gix is actually available.
89	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
90	
91	### [Low→fixed] Two independently-reinvented `PoisonedRunner` test doubles, near-identical
92	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
93	- **Location**: was `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs` and `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`, now `crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`
94	- **Classification**: Maintainability / Duplication
95	- **Fix**: `PoisonedRunner`/`run_git`/`init_repo` consolidated into `callisto-fixtures` (already a workspace dev-dependency), both call sites now import the shared version. `FakeGitTagRunner`/`ScriptedRunner` deliberately left alone — genuinely different test-double shapes, not the same duplication class.
96	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
97	
98	### [Low→fixed] `gix_wasi_spike.rs`'s pinned dev-dependencies were still consuming `cargo-deny` audit budget for a proven-NO-GO path
99	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
100	- **Location**: was `crates/callisto-moon/examples/gix_wasi_spike.rs`
101	- **Classification**: Maintainability / Dead code
102	- **Fix**: spike file and its 12 spike-only pinned `gix-*` dev-dependencies removed; `cargo tree -i gix-odb` confirms only `callisto-vcs`'s real `gix` dependency remains in the tree. The finding itself stays fully documented in this ledger; `runner.rs`'s in-repo pointer updated to reference this ledger instead of the deleted file.
103	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
104	
105	### [Medium→fixed] `apply_version_plan` silently discarded git staging failures, then reported success anyway
106	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
107	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`
108	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
109	- **Fix**: both `git add`/`git rm --cached` call sites now propagate spawn errors via `?` and explicitly check `output.success()`, returning `Err(GraphError::Command(CommandError::Failed{..}))` on failure instead of silently reporting `staged` as populated. Design decision (documented): fatal error, not a nuanced partial-success report — grepped all consumers of `ApplyOutcome.staged` and found none currently branch on it, so a hard error is strictly safer with no behavioral cost.
110	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
111	
112	### [Medium] Per-package git-repo discovery + revwalk in severity inference — O(N_packages × C_commits) instead of O(C_commits)
113	- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-04, performance sweep)
114	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:183-228`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/infer.rs:53-74`, `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs:22-31`
115	- **Classification**: Architectural / Algorithmic complexity
116	- **Root Cause**: `aggregate()` reuses a single `GitRepository` for `resolve_since`, but severity inference is separate — for every package, `fetch_commits` re-discovers the repo and runs its own independent revwalk + tree-diff from HEAD to that package's `since` bound. Most packages share largely the same commit window, so the tree-diff work over the shared range repeats once per package instead of once total.
117	- **Failing Scenario**: 150-package monorepo, most untagged in the last 40 commits — `aggregate()` triggers 150 separate `gix::discover` calls and 150 independent tree-diff walks over an overlapping range, instead of one HEAD walk bucketing each commit's touched paths against all pathspecs at once.
118	- **Fix Status**: unfixed, not yet dispatched. Note: with the `GitDataSource`/`GitAccess` abstraction now in place (see below), `resolve_since` and `fetch_commits` both go through a shared, single-discovery `GitAccess` instance per `aggregate()` call already — this finding is specifically about the per-package *revwalk/tree-diff* work still repeating, not repo re-discovery (that part is already fixed as a byproduct of the trait consolidation).
119	
120	### [Low-Medium→fixed] `ManifestWalkResolver::build` deep-cloned the entire graph just to run the moon-declared-edges crosscheck
121	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
122	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/crosscheck.rs`
123	- **Classification**: Architectural / unnecessary cloning in a hot path
124	- **Fix**: `crosscheck_declared_edges`'s signature changed from `&ManifestWalkResolver` to `&BTreeMap<PackageId, Package>` + `&[DepEdge]` directly; `build()` now calls it against its own local bindings before they're moved into the final resolver — no throwaway resolver, no full-graph clone, confirmed by inspection (no `.clone()` of `packages`/`edges`/either index remains anywhere in the file).
125	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
126	
127	### [Low→fixed] `callisto add` unconditionally built the full graph + tag index even when neither was needed
128	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — fixed at the architecture level, not with a special case
129	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs` (`Workspace`)
130	- **Classification**: Architectural — loads more than the operation needs
131	- **Fix**: `Workspace.tags` changed from an eager field to `OnceCell<TagIndex>`, built lazily on first `Workspace::tags()` call. `add.rs` itself needed zero changes — it only ever touched `ws.root`/`ws.graph.packages()`, so it benefits automatically now that `Workspace::load` no longer forces tag-index construction. All 6 real call sites (`status`/`version`/`tag`×2/`publish`×2) updated to the accessor. Considered making the graph itself lazy too (a second option) but rejected: graph construction needs an external `locator` `Workspace` doesn't store, would broaden the generic surface for only ~2 of 10 command paths, versus tags' zero-new-state, transparent-everywhere win.
132	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
133	
134	### [Medium→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s `DefineExtensionConfigOutput` used a wire-incompatible schema type
135	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
136	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/extension.rs`
137	- **Classification**: Spec Drift / Protocol Mismatch
138	- **Fix**: re-exports moon's real `DefineExtensionConfigOutput{schema: schematic::Schema}` from `moon_pdk_api` (added `schematic`/`schematic_types` as pinned pdk-feature dependencies, matching `moon_pdk_api`'s own pins exactly); `define_extension_config` now returns `Schema::structure(StructType::default())`, preserving the original "deliberately near-empty" intent in the correct type. Verified via a new black-box wasm-sandbox test.
139	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
140	
141	### [Architecture] Formalized the recurring gix-vs-CommandRunner fallback pattern into a real `GitDataSource` trait
142	- **Status**: Landed 2026-08-04 — not a bug fix, a consolidation. Logged here since it directly addresses the root cause behind 5 separate bugs found and fixed earlier this session (`tags.rs`, `commands/tag.rs`, `aggregate.rs`, `window.rs`, plus `changed.rs`'s pre-existing correct instance).
143	- **Location**: new `crates/callisto-vcs/src/{shell.rs, access.rs}`, trait in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`
144	- **Design**: `GitDataSource` trait (`list_tags`/`resolve_commit`/`commits_since`/`create_tag`/`create_floating_major`) with two implementers — `GitRepository` (existing native/gix) and new `ShellGit` (the `CommandRunner`-shelled backend, consolidated from the five hand-rolled duplicates). New `GitAccess` is the selection layer: `GitAccess::discover(root, runner)` tries gix once, applies **asymmetric fallback policy** — reads retry through the shell on any native error, but write ops (`create_tag`/`create_floating_major`) are authoritative once gix is discovered and never masked by a shell retry, preserving the exact invariant `commands/tag.rs`'s original fix established. All five call sites migrated; ~200 lines of duplicated fallback logic removed (e.g. `aggregate.rs`'s `resolve_since` went from a 25-line hand-rolled fallback to a one-line trait call).
145	- **Bundled fix**: `commits_since`'s unbounded-full-history-walk-on-unresolvable-ref bug (previously its own ledger entry) is fixed as part of this consolidation — an unresolved `since_ref` now returns `Err(VcsError::RefNotFound)` in both backends instead of silently walking everything.
146	- **Verified**: `cargo test --workspace` 324/324, plus 15 new tests for the trait/backends themselves (glob rejection, native-vs-shell routing, write-op non-retry, `RefNotFound` propagation).
147	
148	### [Critical→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam is a native-process stub — gix-in-WASM spike ruled out as a fix, host-exec bridge landed
149	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, including real black-box `.wasm` sandbox tests)
150	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
151	- **Classification**: Crash-Safety / Architecture Gap
152	- **Root Cause**: Implemented `CommandRunner` via `std::process::Command::new(program).output()`, which cannot function under WASI sandboxing (WASM guests can't spawn processes). A dedicated spike investigated whether gitoxide's low-level crates could instead read the repo natively from inside the guest (moon does grant a real WASI preopen at `/workspace`) — **NO-GO**: `gix-odb`/`gix-pack`/`gix-index` all read object/index content via `memmap2::Mmap` unconditionally; `memmap2` has no `wasm32-wasip1` backend and its stub returns `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` at runtime. Ref *names* resolve (loose refs use plain `std::fs`), but no object content is readable — confirmed via a real wasmtime run against a real fixture repo, not just static analysis.
153	- **Fix**: `MoonCommandRunner` now bridges through `warpgate_pdk::exec` (the real `#[host_fn] exec_command` binding) on the `pdk` (wasm) build, keeping the original `std::process::Command` path only for native (non-wasm) builds. Verified with genuine black-box coverage: `crates/callisto-moon/tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs` builds the actual `.wasm`, loads it into a real wasmtime-backed Extism sandbox via `moon_pdk_test_utils`, and drives real `register_extension`/`execute_extension` wire calls — not just a type-check.
154	- **Follow-on bug found and fixed during final verification**: the fix's `Cargo.toml` initially declared `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` unconditionally, which made `cargo llvm-cov --all-features` (native, macOS) also attempt a **native** cdylib build/link whenever the `pdk` feature was on, failing on extism-pdk's WASM-host-only import symbols (`_alloc`, `_input_length`, etc. — undefined for native linking). Fixed by removing `crate-type` from the manifest entirely and instead requesting `--crate-type cdylib` explicitly only where the wasm artifact is actually needed (`just wasm-check`, the test's self-bootstrap build) via `cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib`.
155	- **Also found and fixed during final verification**: `moon_pdk_test_utils`'s test-only dependency chain (`warpgate` → `extism` host crate → `wasmtime 41.0.4`) carries several open RUSTSEC advisories (sandbox-escape/miscompile class) plus one unmaintained-crate warning, none of which ship in the production `.wasm` artifact (only the lightweight guest-side `warpgate_pdk` does, which is unaffected). Scoped, documented `[advisories] ignore` added to `deny.toml` for these specific IDs — flagged there as **unstable across consecutive runs** (the RustSec advisory-db itself appears to be actively updated mid-session), so this list may need to grow again on a future CI run.
156	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
157	
158	### [Critical→fixed] `snapshot` wrote a spec-violating version format that defeated its own non-collision invariant
159	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
160	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/snapshot.rs`
161	- **Classification**: Spec Drift
162	- **Fix**: computes one shared `0.0.0-{tag}-{sha7}` value before the per-package loop (was: per-package, `.`-joined, package's-own-version-based). Sha resolution failure now propagates a real `Err(GraphError::Vcs(_))` instead of silently falling back to a fake `"0000000"` sha.
163	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
164	
165	### [Medium→fixed] `commits_since` silently degraded to unbounded full-history walk on unresolvable ref
166	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — fixed as part of the `GitDataSource` trait consolidation (see below)
167	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs` / new `crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs`
168	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback / Unbounded Traversal
169	- **Fix**: an unresolved `since_ref` now returns `Err(VcsError::RefNotFound)` in both the native and shell backends, instead of silently walking full history.
170	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
171	
172	### [Medium→fixed] `list_tags` swallowed a malformed glob pattern and silently matched every tag instead
173	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — confirmed reachable in practice (`TagTemplate::parse` allows `{`/`}` in literal text, so `pkg-a@{version}{oops` parses fine but renders an unclosed-alternate-group glob that `globset` rejects — not theoretical)
174	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs` (`list_tags`), `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (`matching_tags`)
175	- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
176	- **Fix**: glob compile failure now returns `Err(VcsError::InvalidGlob)` / propagates as `GraphError::Vcs(...)` in both places, instead of silently disabling filtering. `None` (no pattern requested at all) still correctly means "match everything" — only compile *failure* is now an error.
177	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
178	
179	### [High→mostly fixed] `PublishOrchestrator`/`RegistryClient` wired into a real `callisto publish` command; `.github` cutover still pending
180	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, orchestrator wiring fixed 2026-08-04
181	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs`, new `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs`, new `callisto publish` CLI command
182	- **Classification**: Dead Code / Architecture Drift
183	- **Root Cause (original)**: `PublishOrchestrator` was fully built/tested but never constructed outside `#[cfg(test)]`; real publishing happened via raw shell `cargo publish`/`npm publish` in `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`, hand-patching problems (rate-limit, idempotency) the Rust orchestrator already solved.
184	- **What changed**: `RegistryClient`'s contract was corrected (after review) to rely entirely on native CLI tools — no HTTP client anywhere. New `SubprocessRegistryClient` wraps `cargo publish`/`npm view`+`npm publish`/`twine upload --skip-existing` via `CommandRunner`, classifying each tool's own bounded output (already-published / rate-limited / auth-failed / other) as the single source of truth per ecosystem — deliberately avoiding a side-channel registry-protocol reimplementation (e.g. no crates.io sparse-index HTTP check) that would itself become a moving target. New `callisto publish` CLI command wires this in, consuming the existing `PublishPlan`.
185	- **Fix Status**: orchestrator + CLI command fixed and tested (mocked `CommandRunner` only, never a real registry call). **`.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s bash publish logic was deliberately left untouched** — the cutover from shell to `callisto publish` is a separate, higher-stakes migration decision (irreversible releases) requiring a staged rollout, not yet scheduled. Known gap: `SubprocessRegistryClient` doesn't yet forward `PublishPlan`'s per-entry `registry`/`tag`/`access` metadata — always targets each ecosystem's default registry.
186	
187	### [Low→fixed] `init` discarded `--yes` entirely, implemented none of the spec's reconcile/diff behavior
188	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
189	- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs`, new `[init]` section in `callisto.toml`, new `InitDiff` type
190	- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Spec Drift
191	- **Fix**: added a lightweight `[init] ecosystems = [...]` bookkeeping section to `callisto.toml` so re-runs have a recorded baseline to diff freshly-discovered state against (drift can't be detected from discovery alone — needed something recorded from the last run). `InitDiff{new_ecosystems, applied}` now carried on `InitReport`. `--yes=false` with drift detected: diff reported, zero file writes. `--yes=true`: applies via a `toml_edit` CST edit touching only the `[init]` table, preserving everything else.
192	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
193	
194	---
195	
196	### [Documentation→fixed] `docs/01-spec.md`'s moon protocol section (§MO.2, §MO.5, §MO.6) described the pre-fix, wire-incompatible types and exec seam
197	- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed 2026-08-04
198	- **Location**: `docs/01-spec.md` §MO.2.1-2.4, §MO.5, §MO.6, one reference in §M.10
199	- **Classification**: Spec Drift (self-inflicted — the spec fell behind the code fixes made earlier this session)
200	- **Fix**: rewrote to match the real, now-fixed `moon_pdk_api` types (Register/Execute/Initialize/DefineExtensionConfig) and the real `warpgate_pdk` exec-seam bridge, each verified against actual current code (file:line) rather than assumed. Added `[SPEC DECISION]` callouts noting these supersede a drafted-before-verification version, matching the doc's existing convention.
201	- **Fix Status**: fixed.
202	
203	## Fixed — 2026-08-04 batch (PEP 440, native git-on-gix unification, moon protocol types, publish orchestrator)
204	
205	- **PEP 440 post+dev combined bump produced a version lower than the input** — `bump.rs`'s `finalize_in_place` condition only checked `is_dev()`, never `is_post()`; a version like `1.2.3.post1.dev1` (which PEP 440 ranks above `1.2.3`) incorrectly finalized to `1.2.3` on a Patch bump. Fixed to only finalize-in-place when there's no post segment.
206	- **PEP 440 non-canonical input broke `Eq`/`Hash`** — `Version` stored the caller's literal `raw` string instead of canonical form; `1.0.0-alpha1` and `1.0.0a1` compared equal via `.compare()` but not via `==`/`Hash`. Fixed by normalizing `raw` to `pep440_rs`'s canonical rendering on parse.
207	- **Git-access inconsistency (gix vs. shelling to the `git` binary)** — `aggregate.rs`'s tag-to-SHA resolution and `callisto-conventional`'s pathspec-scoped commit log both shelled to `git` via `CommandRunner`, inconsistent with `callisto-vcs`'s native `gix` usage everywhere else. Both now go through new `GitRepository::resolve_commit`/`commits_since_with_pathspec` methods — no git-binary shelling left in the native (non-WASM) codebase.
208	- **`callisto-moon` protocol type mismatches (Register/Execute/Initialize)** — see the entries below for what's now fixed vs. still open on the moon front.
209	
210	## Fixed — Batch 2 hardening (landed and verified 2026-08-03, `just ci` green, 178/178 tests)
211	
212	- **Linked-group version convergence** and **pre-release pinned baseline** (`cascade.rs`) — both fixed together; linked members now converge to a single winning target version via `Version::compare`, and pre-release bumps now use `pre.initial_versions` as the pinned base instead of the on-disk value.
213	- **PackageId cross-ecosystem match ambiguity** — `PackageId::matches()` itself left as correct pairwise semantics; the real fix is a new `resolve_target_package()` in `aggregate.rs` used at the one dangerous call site (changeset-to-package resolution), returning `GraphError::AmbiguousName` instead of silently picking a package when a bare name matches two ecosystems.
214	- **CST fidelity**: `CargoToml::open` now strips BOM (defense-in-depth; `toml_edit` 0.22.27 already handled it internally); `PyprojectToml` now fingerprints and restores BOM/CRLF on write, mirroring npm.rs; `write_dependency`'s inline-table/full-table branches now clone/reapply decor.
215	- **Changelog crash-safety**: local `atomic_write` in `callisto-changelog/src/write.rs` replaced with the canonical `callisto_manifests::atomic::atomic_write`.
216	- **4x redundant manifest reads** — now cached across the three read-only open sites (discovery/`publish_targets`/`iter_dependencies`/`base_versions`); the write-open path was deliberately left uncached per the scoped design.
217	- **npm dirty in-memory state on error** — `update_dependency_spec` no longer mutates `overrides`/`resolutions` before validating the target exists.
218	
219	---
220	
221	## Fixed (re-verified 2026-08-03 against current HEAD, no action needed)
222	
223	- **Stale dependency-version rewrite on re-cascade** (`cascade.rs`) — `out.rewrites.entry(key).or_insert(...)` replaced with `out.rewrites.insert(...)` (overwrite); re-escalated packages now correctly overwrite dependents' rewrite entries when the fixpoint drains.
224	- **`compose-pr-body` near-empty output** (`aggregate.rs`, `pr_body.rs`) — `inference.infer(...)` is now actually called and folded in; `PrBodyOptions` (`existing_body`/`labels`/`branch`) is now read.
225	- **`validate.rs` no-op** — loaded changesets now produce real `EmptyChangeset`/`UnknownPackage` diagnostics; `is_valid` is derived from diagnostic severity, not hardcoded.
226	- **`plan-publish` proxy signal** — now runs the real `plan_version` pipeline first; tag-vs-manifest diff is only a fallback for packages absent from the bump plan.
227	- **`--dry-run` never checked** — `transient: global.dry_run` is wired through to `ApplyOptions`; `apply.rs` gates all writes on `!opts.transient`.
228	- **Miette diagnostics dead code** — `main.rs` now prints `miette::Report::new(err)` via `Debug`, which invokes miette's fancy renderer (this is correct, not a plain `Display` dump).
229	
230	---
231	
232	## Known-unverified external claims — resolved
233	
234	- ~~"Silent fallback version defaults" (`cascade.rs:278-297` `unwrap_or_else`)~~ — RESOLVED, stale claim. That code path no longer exists; `bump_target` now uses `ok_or_else` returning a proper `GraphError`, no silent default.
235	- "Pre-release lifecycle verified in `lifecycle_e2e_tests.rs`" — superseded by the new pinned-`initial_versions` finding above; the claimed verification did not catch this.
236	- "Dependency range/catalog constraint calculation verified" — still not independently re-checked.
