# Bug-Hunter Findings Ledger

Append-only log of findings from prior bug-hunter runs. Check this before starting a new sweep so you don't re-spend budget rediscovering the same bug. Update an entry's `Fix Status` in place when it changes — don't delete history, mark it.

Format: one entry per confirmed finding. `Fix Status: unfixed | fix applied, untested | fixed (test run + date)`.

---

### [Medium] PEP 735 Dependency Groups declared supported in spec, entirely unimplemented in code
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-03 sweep)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:183-256` (`iter_dependencies`), `:258-343` (`update_dependency_spec`); spec: `docs/04-python-engine-spec.md:14`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Root Cause**: The Python engine spec lists PEP 735 (`[dependency-groups]`) as one of 5 core PEPs supported. `python.rs` only reads/writes `[project].dependencies` and `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` — no code anywhere references `dependency-groups`.
- **Failing Scenario**: A `pyproject.toml` with `[dependency-groups] test = ["pytest>=7.0"]` pinning an in-workspace sibling — a cascade-triggering bump never rewrites the entry, invisible to cascade/validate/version alike.
- **Fix Status**: unfixed — spec-correction/spec-completion pass dispatched 2026-08-03, code fix not yet started, pending that pass landing.

### [Critical→fixed] `status`/`plan-publish`/`validate` all crashed on the wasm path — `tags.rs` had no CommandRunner fallback
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, real end-to-end wasm sandbox regression test)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (`last_tag_for`, `TagIndex::build`)
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap
- **Root Cause**: `last_tag_for` took an unused `_runner: &R` (`CommandRunner`) parameter and unconditionally called `callisto_vcs::GitRepository::discover(root)?` (gix, native-only). On `wasm32`, `discover` always returns `Err`, so this propagated straight up through `TagIndex::build` and killed `Workspace::load` on the very first package for any real moon invocation — before any actual git logic ran. Found by direct re-reading of `tags.rs`/`changed.rs` after the architecture discussion concluded gix must stay native-only; `changed.rs` already had the correct gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape, `tags.rs` never did.
- **Fix**: `fetch_all_tags` (new) tries gix first, falls through (not `?`) to one `runner.run("git", &["tag","--list"], root)` call when unavailable — mirroring `changed.rs`'s existing pattern exactly, so no new design was invented. Glob-matching against the raw tag list now happens in `callisto-graph` itself (mirroring `callisto-vcs`'s `globset` semantics exactly), so tag selection is byte-identical regardless of which path sourced the list. `TagIndex::build` now fetches the tag list once and reuses it across all packages (was: once per package) — fixes both the wasm32 crash and the O(N) host-round-trip performance gap flagged in the architecture discussion.
- **Verification**: reproduced the crash pre-fix through the real compiled `.wasm` under a real wasmtime sandbox (`exit_code: 1`, `E_GRAPH`, "gix native git operations disabled on WASM target"), confirmed `exit_code: 0` with the correct `lastTag` post-fix — genuine end-to-end evidence, not just a unit test. Also added a call-counting test proving the N→1 batching.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `Version::deserialize` was hardcoded to `VersionGrammar::SemVer`, silently broken for PEP-440-only strings
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — the earlier deferral was revisited with real investigation, not just implemented blind
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Investigation**: grepped every real serde-deserialization call site for a `Version`-bearing type; found exactly one with no available grammar signal — `commands/tag.rs`'s `PublishPlan` ingestion (reads a plan file/stdin from a potentially separate process/CI step, no sibling ecosystem field). Confirmed no PEP-440 `Version` reaches that path *today* (`plan_publish` has no `PublishTarget::Pypi` branch yet), but PyPI/PEP 440 is a fully live, non-stub ecosystem elsewhere in the codebase (manifest parsing, bump logic, and the publish-client classifier are all already implemented) — so this was going to silently break the moment that wiring gap closed.
- **Fix**: `Version::deserialize` now tries `SemVer` first (strictest/most unambiguous), falls back to `Pep440` only if that fails — mirroring `VersionReq::deserialize`'s existing multi-grammar pattern. Residual ambiguity (a string valid under both grammars always resolves to SemVer) is documented directly on the impl and pinned by a test, matching the same accepted tradeoff `VersionReq` already carries.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [High→fixed] `cargo.rs` silently dropped BOM on write despite a comment claiming it was handled
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback (same class as the earlier CST-fidelity fixes; this instance was missed because a code comment incorrectly claimed `toml_edit` handled it internally — that claim was true for the read path, false for the write path)
- **Root Cause**: `CargoToml::open` stripped the BOM before parsing but never recorded that fact; `persist()` wrote `self.document.to_string()` with no BOM restoration.
- **Fix**: Added `has_bom: bool`, populated on open, prepended back on `persist()` — mirrors `python.rs`'s existing pattern. Note: `WorkspaceCargoResolver`'s separate load/persist path was NOT covered by this fix and may have the same latent gap for a workspace-root `Cargo.toml` with a BOM — flagged, not verified either way.
- **Fix Status**: fixed (for `CargoToml` directly; `WorkspaceCargoResolver` unverified).

### [High→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam didn't route a missing-binary host-abort through its own promised `Result` — affected both `execute_extension` and `initialize_extension`
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback / Crash-Safety (falsifies the crate's own "never panics, every failure caught into the report" claim)
- **Root Cause**: When the target program (`moon`/`git`) can't be resolved, `warpgate` 0.30.5's host-side `exec_command` closure returns `Err` from *native* code — Extism aborts the entire plugin call rather than routing it back into the guest as a value the guest's own `Result` handling can see. `MoonCommandRunner::run`'s `Err(e) => classify_host_failure(...)` branch never ran; the whole host call failed instead.
- **Fix**: Pre-check existence via `warpgate_pdk::command_exists` (shells to `which`, not the target program, so a missing program yields an ordinary `false`) before calling `exec`, turning it into the clean `CommandError::NotFound` the method already promised.
- **Fix Status**: fixed. Found only because the new black-box failure-path tests (dispatched to close a coverage gap) immediately falsified the "never panics" claim on first write — exactly the kind of bug happy-path-only testing had been hiding.

### [High→fixed] `callisto add --dry-run` didn't apply `--dry-run` at all — wrote to disk anyway
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (live-tested pre- and post-fix against the built CLI, both text and JSON output formats)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/add.rs`
- **Classification**: Unchecked Flag (same class as the original, already-fixed `version --dry-run` bug — recurred in a sibling command)
- **Fix**: computes and reports the would-be changeset content/path (both output formats) without calling `atomic_write`/`create_dir_all` when `global.dry_run` is set.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `callisto publish`'s output couldn't distinguish "computed a plan" from "actually published packages"
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs`, new `callisto_model::report::PublishReport`
- **Classification**: UX / Missing Feature
- **Fix**: new `PublishReport` type (following the codebase's existing `Plan`-vs-`Report` naming convention) carries per-package `PublishAttempt`/outcome; `PublishOrchestrator::execute` now returns it instead of `()`; the CLI's real (non-dry-run) path prints/returns it instead of re-rendering the input plan.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] `CliError::Io`/`CliError::Registry` lacked `help()` text, inconsistent with `NotATty`'s pattern
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-cli/src/error.rs`
- **Fix**: `Io` converted to a struct variant carrying the failing path (with a manual `From<std::io::Error>` preserving `?`-ergonomics at call sites with no natural path), both variants now have actionable `help()` text. Verified with a real before/after repro (`callisto tag --plan /nonexistent/plan.json`).
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Critical→fixed] `commands/tag.rs`'s `create_tags_with_options` hard-crashed on wasm — same bug class as the original tags.rs crash, not actually fixed everywhere
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (found via exhaustive call-site audit of `GitRepository::discover` prompted by finding the first instance in `tags.rs`)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs`
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Architecture Gap (same class as the already-fixed `tags.rs` bug)
- **Fix**: gix-discovered once at the top of the function; new `tag_exists` (read, gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback, mirrors `tags.rs`) and mutating fallbacks for `create_tag` (`git tag -a`, annotated, no-force) and `create_floating_major` (`git tag -f`, matching gix's exact current semantics) — but for the mutating paths, a real gix failure on a real repo is NOT masked by retrying through the shell (fallback only fires when gix was never discovered at all, not on a genuine gix error).
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [High→fixed] `callisto-conventional`'s `fetch_commits` discarded its `CommandRunner` param — silently dropped conventional-commit inference on wasm
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter
- **Fix**: gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback (mirroring `tags.rs`), new `fetch_commits_via_command_runner` shelling `git log --no-merges --format=\x1e%H\x1f%B <range> [-- <pathspecs>]` (RS/US control-char field separators, immune to misparsing multi-line commit messages; avoided `-z`/NUL-termination since it needs git ≥2.34, above this repo's declared `>=2.20` floor). A malformed/unparseable line now returns `ConventionalError::MalformedGitLogOutput` (a previously-dead-code variant) instead of silently dropping the commit.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `aggregate.rs`'s own `resolve_since` had no `CommandRunner` fallback either — silently degraded to unbounded full-history walk on wasm
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
- **Fix**: same gix-try/`CommandRunner`-fallback shape (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet <tag>^{commit}`), preserving the existing invariant that a real gix `Ok` result (even `Ok(None)`) is authoritative and the `CommandRunner` is never touched when gix is actually available.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] Two independently-reinvented `PoisonedRunner` test doubles, near-identical
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: was `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs` and `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`, now `crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`
- **Classification**: Maintainability / Duplication
- **Fix**: `PoisonedRunner`/`run_git`/`init_repo` consolidated into `callisto-fixtures` (already a workspace dev-dependency), both call sites now import the shared version. `FakeGitTagRunner`/`ScriptedRunner` deliberately left alone — genuinely different test-double shapes, not the same duplication class.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] `gix_wasi_spike.rs`'s pinned dev-dependencies were still consuming `cargo-deny` audit budget for a proven-NO-GO path
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: was `crates/callisto-moon/examples/gix_wasi_spike.rs`
- **Classification**: Maintainability / Dead code
- **Fix**: spike file and its 12 spike-only pinned `gix-*` dev-dependencies removed; `cargo tree -i gix-odb` confirms only `callisto-vcs`'s real `gix` dependency remains in the tree. The finding itself stays fully documented in this ledger; `runner.rs`'s in-repo pointer updated to reference this ledger instead of the deleted file.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `apply_version_plan` silently discarded git staging failures, then reported success anyway
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
- **Fix**: both `git add`/`git rm --cached` call sites now propagate spawn errors via `?` and explicitly check `output.success()`, returning `Err(GraphError::Command(CommandError::Failed{..}))` on failure instead of silently reporting `staged` as populated. Design decision (documented): fatal error, not a nuanced partial-success report — grepped all consumers of `ApplyOutcome.staged` and found none currently branch on it, so a hard error is strictly safer with no behavioral cost.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium] Per-package git-repo discovery + revwalk in severity inference — O(N_packages × C_commits) instead of O(C_commits)
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (2026-08-04, performance sweep)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:183-228`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/infer.rs:53-74`, `crates/callisto-conventional/src/window.rs:22-31`
- **Classification**: Architectural / Algorithmic complexity
- **Root Cause**: `aggregate()` reuses a single `GitRepository` for `resolve_since`, but severity inference is separate — for every package, `fetch_commits` re-discovers the repo and runs its own independent revwalk + tree-diff from HEAD to that package's `since` bound. Most packages share largely the same commit window, so the tree-diff work over the shared range repeats once per package instead of once total.
- **Failing Scenario**: 150-package monorepo, most untagged in the last 40 commits — `aggregate()` triggers 150 separate `gix::discover` calls and 150 independent tree-diff walks over an overlapping range, instead of one HEAD walk bucketing each commit's touched paths against all pathspecs at once.
- **Fix Status**: unfixed, not yet dispatched. Note: with the `GitDataSource`/`GitAccess` abstraction now in place (see below), `resolve_since` and `fetch_commits` both go through a shared, single-discovery `GitAccess` instance per `aggregate()` call already — this finding is specifically about the per-package *revwalk/tree-diff* work still repeating, not repo re-discovery (that part is already fixed as a byproduct of the trait consolidation).

### [Low-Medium→fixed] `ManifestWalkResolver::build` deep-cloned the entire graph just to run the moon-declared-edges crosscheck
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/crosscheck.rs`
- **Classification**: Architectural / unnecessary cloning in a hot path
- **Fix**: `crosscheck_declared_edges`'s signature changed from `&ManifestWalkResolver` to `&BTreeMap<PackageId, Package>` + `&[DepEdge]` directly; `build()` now calls it against its own local bindings before they're moved into the final resolver — no throwaway resolver, no full-graph clone, confirmed by inspection (no `.clone()` of `packages`/`edges`/either index remains anywhere in the file).
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Low→fixed] `callisto add` unconditionally built the full graph + tag index even when neither was needed
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — fixed at the architecture level, not with a special case
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs` (`Workspace`)
- **Classification**: Architectural — loads more than the operation needs
- **Fix**: `Workspace.tags` changed from an eager field to `OnceCell<TagIndex>`, built lazily on first `Workspace::tags()` call. `add.rs` itself needed zero changes — it only ever touched `ws.root`/`ws.graph.packages()`, so it benefits automatically now that `Workspace::load` no longer forces tag-index construction. All 6 real call sites (`status`/`version`/`tag`×2/`publish`×2) updated to the accessor. Considered making the graph itself lazy too (a second option) but rejected: graph construction needs an external `locator` `Workspace` doesn't store, would broaden the generic surface for only ~2 of 10 command paths, versus tags' zero-new-state, transparent-everywhere win.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s `DefineExtensionConfigOutput` used a wire-incompatible schema type
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/extension.rs`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift / Protocol Mismatch
- **Fix**: re-exports moon's real `DefineExtensionConfigOutput{schema: schematic::Schema}` from `moon_pdk_api` (added `schematic`/`schematic_types` as pinned pdk-feature dependencies, matching `moon_pdk_api`'s own pins exactly); `define_extension_config` now returns `Schema::structure(StructType::default())`, preserving the original "deliberately near-empty" intent in the correct type. Verified via a new black-box wasm-sandbox test.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Architecture] Formalized the recurring gix-vs-CommandRunner fallback pattern into a real `GitDataSource` trait
- **Status**: Landed 2026-08-04 — not a bug fix, a consolidation. Logged here since it directly addresses the root cause behind 5 separate bugs found and fixed earlier this session (`tags.rs`, `commands/tag.rs`, `aggregate.rs`, `window.rs`, plus `changed.rs`'s pre-existing correct instance).
- **Location**: new `crates/callisto-vcs/src/{shell.rs, access.rs}`, trait in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`
- **Design**: `GitDataSource` trait (`list_tags`/`resolve_commit`/`commits_since`/`create_tag`/`create_floating_major`) with two implementers — `GitRepository` (existing native/gix) and new `ShellGit` (the `CommandRunner`-shelled backend, consolidated from the five hand-rolled duplicates). New `GitAccess` is the selection layer: `GitAccess::discover(root, runner)` tries gix once, applies **asymmetric fallback policy** — reads retry through the shell on any native error, but write ops (`create_tag`/`create_floating_major`) are authoritative once gix is discovered and never masked by a shell retry, preserving the exact invariant `commands/tag.rs`'s original fix established. All five call sites migrated; ~200 lines of duplicated fallback logic removed (e.g. `aggregate.rs`'s `resolve_since` went from a 25-line hand-rolled fallback to a one-line trait call).
- **Bundled fix**: `commits_since`'s unbounded-full-history-walk-on-unresolvable-ref bug (previously its own ledger entry) is fixed as part of this consolidation — an unresolved `since_ref` now returns `Err(VcsError::RefNotFound)` in both backends instead of silently walking everything.
- **Verified**: `cargo test --workspace` 324/324, plus 15 new tests for the trait/backends themselves (glob rejection, native-vs-shell routing, write-op non-retry, `RefNotFound` propagation).

### [Critical→fixed] `callisto-moon`'s exec seam is a native-process stub — gix-in-WASM spike ruled out as a fix, host-exec bridge landed
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 (`just ci` green, including real black-box `.wasm` sandbox tests)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs`
- **Classification**: Crash-Safety / Architecture Gap
- **Root Cause**: Implemented `CommandRunner` via `std::process::Command::new(program).output()`, which cannot function under WASI sandboxing (WASM guests can't spawn processes). A dedicated spike investigated whether gitoxide's low-level crates could instead read the repo natively from inside the guest (moon does grant a real WASI preopen at `/workspace`) — **NO-GO**: `gix-odb`/`gix-pack`/`gix-index` all read object/index content via `memmap2::Mmap` unconditionally; `memmap2` has no `wasm32-wasip1` backend and its stub returns `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` at runtime. Ref *names* resolve (loose refs use plain `std::fs`), but no object content is readable — confirmed via a real wasmtime run against a real fixture repo, not just static analysis.
- **Fix**: `MoonCommandRunner` now bridges through `warpgate_pdk::exec` (the real `#[host_fn] exec_command` binding) on the `pdk` (wasm) build, keeping the original `std::process::Command` path only for native (non-wasm) builds. Verified with genuine black-box coverage: `crates/callisto-moon/tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs` builds the actual `.wasm`, loads it into a real wasmtime-backed Extism sandbox via `moon_pdk_test_utils`, and drives real `register_extension`/`execute_extension` wire calls — not just a type-check.
- **Follow-on bug found and fixed during final verification**: the fix's `Cargo.toml` initially declared `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` unconditionally, which made `cargo llvm-cov --all-features` (native, macOS) also attempt a **native** cdylib build/link whenever the `pdk` feature was on, failing on extism-pdk's WASM-host-only import symbols (`_alloc`, `_input_length`, etc. — undefined for native linking). Fixed by removing `crate-type` from the manifest entirely and instead requesting `--crate-type cdylib` explicitly only where the wasm artifact is actually needed (`just wasm-check`, the test's self-bootstrap build) via `cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib`.
- **Also found and fixed during final verification**: `moon_pdk_test_utils`'s test-only dependency chain (`warpgate` → `extism` host crate → `wasmtime 41.0.4`) carries several open RUSTSEC advisories (sandbox-escape/miscompile class) plus one unmaintained-crate warning, none of which ship in the production `.wasm` artifact (only the lightweight guest-side `warpgate_pdk` does, which is unaffected). Scoped, documented `[advisories] ignore` added to `deny.toml` for these specific IDs — flagged there as **unstable across consecutive runs** (the RustSec advisory-db itself appears to be actively updated mid-session), so this list may need to grow again on a future CI run.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Critical→fixed] `snapshot` wrote a spec-violating version format that defeated its own non-collision invariant
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/snapshot.rs`
- **Classification**: Spec Drift
- **Fix**: computes one shared `0.0.0-{tag}-{sha7}` value before the per-package loop (was: per-package, `.`-joined, package's-own-version-based). Sha resolution failure now propagates a real `Err(GraphError::Vcs(_))` instead of silently falling back to a fake `"0000000"` sha.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `commits_since` silently degraded to unbounded full-history walk on unresolvable ref
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — fixed as part of the `GitDataSource` trait consolidation (see below)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs` / new `crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs`
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback / Unbounded Traversal
- **Fix**: an unresolved `since_ref` now returns `Err(VcsError::RefNotFound)` in both the native and shell backends, instead of silently walking full history.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [Medium→fixed] `list_tags` swallowed a malformed glob pattern and silently matched every tag instead
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04 — confirmed reachable in practice (`TagTemplate::parse` allows `{`/`}` in literal text, so `pkg-a@{version}{oops` parses fine but renders an unclosed-alternate-group glob that `globset` rejects — not theoretical)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs` (`list_tags`), `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (`matching_tags`)
- **Classification**: Silent Fallback
- **Fix**: glob compile failure now returns `Err(VcsError::InvalidGlob)` / propagates as `GraphError::Vcs(...)` in both places, instead of silently disabling filtering. `None` (no pattern requested at all) still correctly means "match everything" — only compile *failure* is now an error.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

### [High→mostly fixed] `PublishOrchestrator`/`RegistryClient` wired into a real `callisto publish` command; `.github` cutover still pending
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, orchestrator wiring fixed 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs`, new `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs`, new `callisto publish` CLI command
- **Classification**: Dead Code / Architecture Drift
- **Root Cause (original)**: `PublishOrchestrator` was fully built/tested but never constructed outside `#[cfg(test)]`; real publishing happened via raw shell `cargo publish`/`npm publish` in `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`, hand-patching problems (rate-limit, idempotency) the Rust orchestrator already solved.
- **What changed**: `RegistryClient`'s contract was corrected (after review) to rely entirely on native CLI tools — no HTTP client anywhere. New `SubprocessRegistryClient` wraps `cargo publish`/`npm view`+`npm publish`/`twine upload --skip-existing` via `CommandRunner`, classifying each tool's own bounded output (already-published / rate-limited / auth-failed / other) as the single source of truth per ecosystem — deliberately avoiding a side-channel registry-protocol reimplementation (e.g. no crates.io sparse-index HTTP check) that would itself become a moving target. New `callisto publish` CLI command wires this in, consuming the existing `PublishPlan`.
- **Fix Status**: orchestrator + CLI command fixed and tested (mocked `CommandRunner` only, never a real registry call). **`.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s bash publish logic was deliberately left untouched** — the cutover from shell to `callisto publish` is a separate, higher-stakes migration decision (irreversible releases) requiring a staged rollout, not yet scheduled. Known gap: `SubprocessRegistryClient` doesn't yet forward `PublishPlan`'s per-entry `registry`/`tag`/`access` metadata — always targets each ecosystem's default registry.

### [Low→fixed] `init` discarded `--yes` entirely, implemented none of the spec's reconcile/diff behavior
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed and verified 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs`, new `[init]` section in `callisto.toml`, new `InitDiff` type
- **Classification**: Discarded Parameter / Spec Drift
- **Fix**: added a lightweight `[init] ecosystems = [...]` bookkeeping section to `callisto.toml` so re-runs have a recorded baseline to diff freshly-discovered state against (drift can't be detected from discovery alone — needed something recorded from the last run). `InitDiff{new_ecosystems, applied}` now carried on `InitReport`. `--yes=false` with drift detected: diff reported, zero file writes. `--yes=true`: applies via a `toml_edit` CST edit touching only the `[init]` table, preserving everything else.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

---

### [Documentation→fixed] `docs/01-spec.md`'s moon protocol section (§MO.2, §MO.5, §MO.6) described the pre-fix, wire-incompatible types and exec seam
- **Status**: CONFIRMED, fixed 2026-08-04
- **Location**: `docs/01-spec.md` §MO.2.1-2.4, §MO.5, §MO.6, one reference in §M.10
- **Classification**: Spec Drift (self-inflicted — the spec fell behind the code fixes made earlier this session)
- **Fix**: rewrote to match the real, now-fixed `moon_pdk_api` types (Register/Execute/Initialize/DefineExtensionConfig) and the real `warpgate_pdk` exec-seam bridge, each verified against actual current code (file:line) rather than assumed. Added `[SPEC DECISION]` callouts noting these supersede a drafted-before-verification version, matching the doc's existing convention.
- **Fix Status**: fixed.

## Fixed — 2026-08-04 batch (PEP 440, native git-on-gix unification, moon protocol types, publish orchestrator)

- **PEP 440 post+dev combined bump produced a version lower than the input** — `bump.rs`'s `finalize_in_place` condition only checked `is_dev()`, never `is_post()`; a version like `1.2.3.post1.dev1` (which PEP 440 ranks above `1.2.3`) incorrectly finalized to `1.2.3` on a Patch bump. Fixed to only finalize-in-place when there's no post segment.
- **PEP 440 non-canonical input broke `Eq`/`Hash`** — `Version` stored the caller's literal `raw` string instead of canonical form; `1.0.0-alpha1` and `1.0.0a1` compared equal via `.compare()` but not via `==`/`Hash`. Fixed by normalizing `raw` to `pep440_rs`'s canonical rendering on parse.
- **Git-access inconsistency (gix vs. shelling to the `git` binary)** — `aggregate.rs`'s tag-to-SHA resolution and `callisto-conventional`'s pathspec-scoped commit log both shelled to `git` via `CommandRunner`, inconsistent with `callisto-vcs`'s native `gix` usage everywhere else. Both now go through new `GitRepository::resolve_commit`/`commits_since_with_pathspec` methods — no git-binary shelling left in the native (non-WASM) codebase.
- **`callisto-moon` protocol type mismatches (Register/Execute/Initialize)** — see the entries below for what's now fixed vs. still open on the moon front.

## Fixed — Batch 2 hardening (landed and verified 2026-08-03, `just ci` green, 178/178 tests)

- **Linked-group version convergence** and **pre-release pinned baseline** (`cascade.rs`) — both fixed together; linked members now converge to a single winning target version via `Version::compare`, and pre-release bumps now use `pre.initial_versions` as the pinned base instead of the on-disk value.
- **PackageId cross-ecosystem match ambiguity** — `PackageId::matches()` itself left as correct pairwise semantics; the real fix is a new `resolve_target_package()` in `aggregate.rs` used at the one dangerous call site (changeset-to-package resolution), returning `GraphError::AmbiguousName` instead of silently picking a package when a bare name matches two ecosystems.
- **CST fidelity**: `CargoToml::open` now strips BOM (defense-in-depth; `toml_edit` 0.22.27 already handled it internally); `PyprojectToml` now fingerprints and restores BOM/CRLF on write, mirroring npm.rs; `write_dependency`'s inline-table/full-table branches now clone/reapply decor.
- **Changelog crash-safety**: local `atomic_write` in `callisto-changelog/src/write.rs` replaced with the canonical `callisto_manifests::atomic::atomic_write`.
- **4x redundant manifest reads** — now cached across the three read-only open sites (discovery/`publish_targets`/`iter_dependencies`/`base_versions`); the write-open path was deliberately left uncached per the scoped design.
- **npm dirty in-memory state on error** — `update_dependency_spec` no longer mutates `overrides`/`resolutions` before validating the target exists.

---

## Fixed (re-verified 2026-08-03 against current HEAD, no action needed)

- **Stale dependency-version rewrite on re-cascade** (`cascade.rs`) — `out.rewrites.entry(key).or_insert(...)` replaced with `out.rewrites.insert(...)` (overwrite); re-escalated packages now correctly overwrite dependents' rewrite entries when the fixpoint drains.
- **`compose-pr-body` near-empty output** (`aggregate.rs`, `pr_body.rs`) — `inference.infer(...)` is now actually called and folded in; `PrBodyOptions` (`existing_body`/`labels`/`branch`) is now read.
- **`validate.rs` no-op** — loaded changesets now produce real `EmptyChangeset`/`UnknownPackage` diagnostics; `is_valid` is derived from diagnostic severity, not hardcoded.
- **`plan-publish` proxy signal** — now runs the real `plan_version` pipeline first; tag-vs-manifest diff is only a fallback for packages absent from the bump plan.
- **`--dry-run` never checked** — `transient: global.dry_run` is wired through to `ApplyOptions`; `apply.rs` gates all writes on `!opts.transient`.
- **Miette diagnostics dead code** — `main.rs` now prints `miette::Report::new(err)` via `Debug`, which invokes miette's fancy renderer (this is correct, not a plain `Display` dump).

---

## Known-unverified external claims — resolved

- ~~"Silent fallback version defaults" (`cascade.rs:278-297` `unwrap_or_else`)~~ — RESOLVED, stale claim. That code path no longer exists; `bump_target` now uses `ok_or_else` returning a proper `GraphError`, no silent default.
- "Pre-release lifecycle verified in `lifecycle_e2e_tests.rs`" — superseded by the new pinned-`initial_versions` finding above; the claimed verification did not catch this.
- "Dependency range/catalog constraint calculation verified" — still not independently re-checked.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates
# Specifications

Each spec (`spec@1`) states current behavior as testable criteria, grouped by topic prefix. No history: Git records how the behavior got here, and [`docs/adr/`](../adr/README.md) records the design decisions that still hold.

| Spec | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [`workspace.json`](workspace.json) | Root and member discovery, package identity, per-package config rules, npm platform packages |
| [`versioning.json`](versioning.json) | Changeset format, severity aggregation, cascade, groups, prerelease, snapshot, applying versions, changelogs, the release decision file |
| [`release.json`](release.json) | `callisto release`, the CI route, decision authority, operation order, registry publish and observation, reruns, tags and GitHub releases, the managed release PR |
| [`cli.json`](cli.json) | Command surface, output and exit codes, `status`, `add`, `init`, generated workflows, `pre`, `snapshot`, `completions`, `schema` |
| [`matrix.json`](matrix.json) | `callisto matrix`: native build targets and runtime constraints for CI |

`REQ-DX-V1.md` is the open v1 requirement; delete it when v1 ships.

How the code implements these specs: [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) and [`docs/architecture/`](../architecture/).

When code and a spec disagree, reproduce the behavior first. Fix the spec if the intended contract changed; otherwise fix the code.

Known failing contracts and unverified integrations are recorded in [V1-FINDINGS](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md), not converted into successful exceptions. Proposed canonical-reference, version-authority and required-output behavior lives in [the scoped design](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md) and [sequencing plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json). Amend the matching current-behavior spec in the same change that implements it; these documents do not make future behavior current.
# REQ-DX-V1: world-class release DX and correctness for v1

Stakeholder: Callisto owner (sole maintainer); users releasing Rust, npm (incl. napi-rs) and Python monorepos.

Status: open. The command surface and release machinery exist, but verified correctness and integration gaps remain. [The findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md) records evidence and coverage; [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [sequencing plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json) track the work. Cargo real-registry tests now exist; they do not establish full production release-path coverage.

Why: Callisto's release engine is rigorous but its surface is confusing and its setup is heavy. Goal: a new repo goes from `callisto init` to its first published release in under 10 minutes, with one obvious release command and no known correctness bugs.

## Decided by the owner

- The main verb is `release`. Flow: `add` → `version` → `release`.
- `callisto release` publishes every package whose version has no release yet: registry publish, tag, forge release. `--dry-run` previews it on any branch.
- User-facing commands shown in `--help`: init, add, status, version, release, pre, snapshot, completions. Plumbing stays callable but hidden.
- `add` keeps both modes: interactive wizard on a TTY, flags for automation, clear error with the needed flags when neither.
- Breaking changes are fine pre-1.0; no external users.
- Current implementation scope is Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm (including napi-rs) and Python/PyPI. Keep architecture room for Go and C#/.NET/NuGet without implementing those adapters now.
- Prefer canonical ecosystem-qualified references and deliberate legacy migration over collision-triggered identity magic. Release ownership, native distribution identity, version authority and effects are separate responsibilities; the detailed proposal is [the scoped model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- Do not build a universal package manager, build scheduler, cross-language inference engine or persisted execution journal. Native tools/CI own compilation, packing and authentication.

## Done when

- `callisto --help` lists exactly the 8 user commands; each has one plain-language line.
- `callisto release --dry-run` with no flags prints the full plan on any branch; `callisto release` with no flags performs it locally with credentials in the environment.
- The CI split (plan → build → execute across jobs) works through `release` flags or hidden subcommands, and callisto's own workflow uses them.
- `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag`, `filter-plan` are removed; one plan implementation serves preview and execution and includes every check listed above.
- Text output uses colour/tables on a TTY, plain text when piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, no schema versions in text; `status` shows cascaded bumps.
- Verified defects in the findings register are fixed with regression coverage across affected siblings. CI runs the shipped runtime behavior; no shipped Cargo feature variants. Existing real local npm/Cargo/PyPI tests are retained, with skipped prerequisites distinguished from executed coverage and production binding/observation paths checked separately.
- `callisto init` detects ecosystems/packages, asks only intent (fixed vs independent; release artifacts if binaries exist), writes minimal config, and can write a GitHub workflow using `callisto-action` of <= 40 lines; a non-interactive mode exists.
- Supported fixtures cover separate native packages, dual Cargo/npm outputs, and the common co-located Cargo/Maturin version-authority case. Native dependency ranges/names, all affected lockfiles and built distribution metadata agree after versioning.
- A retry completes required missing effects without inventing a new version, even after tag creation or a partial Python/platform upload. Required outputs and shared public-announcement prerequisites are explicit; version/tag existence alone is not completion evidence.
- Generated workflows build/place only intended supported outputs and configure native authentication without registry secrets in plan/build jobs. This repo retains no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate; the reviewed merge remains the authorization.
- Fresh-repository runs measure init-to-first-publication against the existing under-ten-minute goal, including commit and credential steps. The supported/unsupported boundary is documented; no timing evidence is claimed until measured.

## Decisions still open

Authenticated private Python indexes and HTML-only indexes; npm dist-tag verification/promotion; universal registry checksum requirements; wrapper-specific bump severity; inferred-only/manual release commits under ADR 2; exact canonical-reference migration and release-owner wire representation. Record those choices before their implementation; do not make unstated preferences release gates.

Go major-qualified module paths/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are model examples, not promised runtime support or additional v1 gates.

## Out of scope

- Non-GitHub forges (later).
- Moon plugin (replaced by a proto plugin separately).
- Crate consolidation / license split.
- Production Go or NuGet adapters, arbitrary SCM-derived Python version backends, automatic foreign-registry dependency inference and cross-registry atomic rollback.

# Configuration reference

Every key `callisto.toml` accepts, from `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/{raw,resolve,groups}.rs`. Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`).

This reference describes current keys, not the [proposed canonical-identity/polyglot design](architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Exact references can currently be bare or qualified; prefer `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` and `pypi/name` when writing new configuration. No release-owner, generic build-input or per-file PyPI configuration is implemented yet.

## Top-level tables

| Table | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
| `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
| `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
| `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
| `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
| `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package exact-match overrides |
| `[[package-set]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package glob-match overrides |
| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |
| `[init]` | table | no | Deprecated; parsed for compatibility, never read |

## `[changesets]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |

Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.

## `[cascade]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
| `peer-escalation` | bool | `true` | Escalate peer-dependency bumps into the cascade |
| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true
```

## `[validation]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |

## `[release]`

Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
| `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |
| `[release.profiles]` | table | none | Legacy; only `profiles.production` is read, to migrate its `forge-repository` into the top-level key. Conflicting values between the two are a hard error. |

### `[[release.artifact]]`

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
```

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name. Two entries exist by default even with no `[registries]` table at all: `crates-io` (kind `cargo`) and `npm` (kind `npm`), both with no URL override.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | `"npm"` if omitted | Registry ecosystem |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |

An explicit registry entry still defaults `kind` to npm when omitted; requiring it is planned. For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
```

## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`

Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact `PackageId` (first matching rule wins, prefixed forms like `cargo/foo` take priority over bare `foo` regardless of declaration order). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is a glob `PackagePattern` and can match many packages at once; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact ecosystem-qualified id or bare name. `[[package-set]]`: glob pattern. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`

Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | Package names in the group |

`[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = ["callisto-model", "callisto-manifests", "callisto-graph", "callisto-cli"]
```

## `[init]`

Deprecated. `ecosystems` (array of strings) is parsed so older config files still load, but nothing reads it.

## Identity and defaults

Unspecified package fields are filled during graph construction: the release trigger defaults to changesets, the changelog to the package directory, and publish targets to those declared by its manifests. Default tags use the display id, so newly created tags become qualified after name promotion; historical bare tags use the ownership fallback described in [identity](architecture/identity.md). Canonical references alone do not repair the open rename/demotion failures.

| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |
| `[init]` | table | no | Deprecated; parsed for compatibility, never read |

## `[changesets]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |

Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.

## `[cascade]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
| `peer-escalation` | bool | `true` | Escalate peer-dependency bumps into the cascade |
| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true
```

## `[validation]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |

## `[release]`

Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
| `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |
| `[release.profiles]` | table | none | Legacy; only `profiles.production` is read, to migrate its `forge-repository` into the top-level key. Conflicting values between the two are a hard error. |

### `[[release.artifact]]`

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
```

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name. Two entries exist by default even with no `[registries]` table at all: `crates-io` (kind `cargo`) and `npm` (kind `npm`), both with no URL override.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | `"npm"` if omitted | Registry ecosystem |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |

An explicit registry entry still defaults `kind` to npm when omitted; requiring it is planned. For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
```

## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`

Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact `PackageId` (first matching rule wins, prefixed forms like `cargo/foo` take priority over bare `foo` regardless of declaration order). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is a glob `PackagePattern` and can match many packages at once; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact ecosystem-qualified id or bare name. `[[package-set]]`: glob pattern. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`

Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | Package names in the group |

`[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = ["callisto-model", "callisto-manifests", "callisto-graph", "callisto-cli"]
```

## `[init]`

Deprecated. `ecosystems` (array of strings) is parsed so older config files still load, but nothing reads it.

## Identity and defaults

Unspecified package fields are filled during graph construction: the release trigger defaults to changesets, the changelog to the package directory, and publish targets to those declared by its manifests. Default tags use the display id, so newly created tags become qualified after name promotion; historical bare tags use the ownership fallback described in [identity](architecture/identity.md). Canonical references alone do not repair the open rename/demotion failures.

# Publishing: registry authentication

Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).

Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.

---

## npm

Two supported patterns.

### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`

Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with npm registry
  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  env:
    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
```

`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.

### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`

`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: '20'
    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.

### Choosing a pattern

| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
| Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |

### Provenance

Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.

---

## Cargo (crates.io)

Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:

```yaml
env:
  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
```

Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. In this repo, inject it only into `execute`.

---

## Python (PyPI)

Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):

```yaml
env:
  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
```

Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.

Map the generated workflow's `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_PASSWORD` in the publishing job. The secret name alone does not configure Twine.

### Generated Callisto workflows

Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.

Native publish hooks, including `prepare` and `prepublishOnly`, run unchanged with their usual publishing environment.

### Current Python support limits

Callisto supports static PEP 621 or Poetry versions with `python -m build` and Twine. Current limits:

- Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
- Without a sealed build, files an earlier attempt uploaded are matched by name, not by content: a rebuild is not always byte-identical. A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
- A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
- A release can only be completed for 14 days after its first file; after that, PyPI [refuses new files](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/) and the release needs a new version.
- A package tagged by an earlier version of callisto with only some of its files uploaded is reported as released when rerun at the same commit. Finish it by uploading the missing files with `twine`.
- A configured `url` is the simple index Callisto reads and, unless `publish-url` names another endpoint, the one Twine uploads to. Private indexes with read authentication or HTML-only responses need explicit support. Twine credentials do not authenticate `curl`.
- Dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`, Poetry groups and the legacy dev-dependency tables are not followed or rewritten when a workspace package is released. Under uv a version pin on a workspace member is ignored, and Poetry normally references siblings by path, so a stale pin there is harmless; a group that pins a registry version of a sibling is not updated.
- Snapshots use a PEP 440 local label (`0.0.0.dev0+<tag>.<sha>`), which public PyPI rejects. See [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).
# Releasing

How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.

For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).

---

## Local release: `callisto release`

`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.

- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
- `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.

`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.

### Current retry limit

If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` can print `Nothing to release.` without a receipt.

- That message is not proof of completion.
- Generated simple workflows share this limit.
- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.

---

## Generated workflows

`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.

Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.

- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.

Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

Generated build support has these boundaries:

- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.

The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.

Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build/placement roster is currently workspace-wide, not narrowed to the release intent. Unrelated addons can block a release; this is tracked for correction, not a support requirement.
- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

## PR pre-flight verification

[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:

- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.

---

## Release identity and recovery

Every release run records two different revisions:

- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.

A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and an explicit full release-source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code, create a version PR, or invent a newer version.

To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs". Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh
gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

## Publication checks

Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.

Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.

---

## Platform-package publish order

`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.

A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.

- **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.

For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.
# How Callisto works

Callisto turns changesets and native package metadata into a version plan. It then coordinates the selected registry, Git, and GitHub operations. Current scope is Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI.

## Where it fits

Use Callisto when contributors should declare release impact and a repo needs native dependency updates across its supported package types. The version plan makes each bump reviewable before publication.

Other tools may fit your existing workflow:

- [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) focuses on npm package releases.
- [Knope](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/) offers configurable release workflows.
- [Nx Release](https://nx.dev/docs/features/manage-releases) integrates with Nx projects and tasks.
- [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/design.md) builds release PRs from conventional commits.

## A change through the system

Suppose a Cargo crate `service` depends on `core`. A contributor records a change to `core`:

```sh
callisto add --package cargo/core:minor --summary "Add streaming API"
callisto status
callisto version --dry-run
```

Callisto builds the version plan from the changeset, manifests, and `callisto.toml`:

- The changeset requests a minor bump for `core`.
- The Cargo dependency in `service` tells Callisto whether the new version fits its existing requirement.
  - Under the default `out-of-range` policy, a version outside that requirement can bump `service` and update its dependency declaration.
  - Cascade mode and bump severity are configurable.
- Fixed and linked groups can add packages through explicit policy.
- Unrelated npm and Python packages do not join solely because they share the repo.

After reviewing the plan, `callisto version` updates affected manifests, lockfiles, and changelogs. It stages the versioned state for a commit. `callisto release --dry-run` then previews the release operations.

## The model

| Concept | What it means today |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace package | A dependency graph node located from source and manifests. |
| Distribution | A native Cargo, npm, or PyPI identity described by a manifest. One package can expose multiple supported distributions. |
| Native dependency | A manifest relationship that can affect dependent versions and publication order. |
| Version group | An explicit fixed or linked rule in `callisto.toml`. |
| Release operation | One registry, tag, GitHub release, or asset effect with prerequisites. |

These relationships serve different purposes. For example, a Rust library embedded in a Python wheel is a build input. That alone does not create a Cargo registry dependency or make the crate and wheel share a version. See [configuration](config.md) for supported dependency and version-group rules.

## Releasing and recovery

- **Local release:** `callisto release --dry-run` previews the plan. `callisto release` runs it from a clean checkout.
  - Native publishers use their own credentials.
- **Managed CI:** The version PR commits the selected package and version decision. CI verifies it after merge.
  - Planning declares operations. Building creates artifacts. Execution receives registry credentials.
- **Execution:** Callisto checks each provider before acting.
  - It adopts an exact match, performs and confirms an absent effect, and stops on a conflict or indeterminate result.
  - A receipt records the evidence collected.

Release operations follow known dependency and platform prerequisites. They do not follow a fixed Cargo, npm, then PyPI sequence. The [release guide](releasing.md) covers the local and CI paths, retries, and recovery.

## Current support

Callisto is pre-v1. These rows describe current behavior rather than planned adapters.

| Ecosystem | Versioning | Publishing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cargo | Crate versions, supported dependency declarations, lockfiles | Cargo |
| npm/pnpm | Package versions, supported native dependency forms, lockfiles | Native npm tooling |
| Python/PyPI | Static PEP 621 or Poetry versions | Build backend and Twine |

| Layout | Current boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Cargo product binaries | Generated CI builds discovered Cargo binary targets. Other products need a user authored builder. |
| napi platform packages | Generated CI supports configured targets. Its workspace wide roster can include unrelated addons. |
| Co-located Cargo and Maturin | Discovery fails; no generated Maturin workflow. |
| Custom product assets | Declared artifact slots can use a manual CI builder and Callisto's execute route. |

Known release limits matter when choosing a workflow:

- A multi-registry release is not atomic.
- A tag does not yet prove that every distribution from one source package was published.
- A fresh local retry can skip unfinished work after creating a tag.
- PyPI observation does not yet prove that every intended wheel and sdist was uploaded.
- Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Go and NuGet publishers are not available.

Package owners control native lifecycle hooks. Callisto invokes supported tools without rewriting those hooks. See [publishing](publishing.md) for credentials and Python index limits, and [releasing](releasing.md) for the complete operation and recovery rules.
